# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

FileData::hashCode
Summary:
Computes a hash code consistent with FileData equality.
Algorithm:
1. Compute a combined hash from content and mimeType.
2. Use both fields so that equal objects produce the same hash.
3. Return the resulting integer.
Related Features:
- content
- mimeType
Related Classes: FileData
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Integer hash code.
Pre-condition:
- None.
Post-condition:
- Equal FileData objects yield equal hash codes.

FileData::equals
Summary:
Determines whether two FileData instances are value-equal.
Algorithm:
1. Return true if both references point to the same object.
2. Return false if the other object is null or of a different type.
3. Compare content and mimeType for equality.
4. Return true only if both fields are equal.
Related Features:
- content
- mimeType
Related Classes: FileData
Input:
- o: object to compare against.
Output:
- boolean indicating whether the two objects represent the same file data value.
Pre-condition:
- None.
Post-condition:
- The comparison does not modify either object.
- Equality is based on content and mimeType.

You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary:
Computes encoding statistics for an original text and its emoji-encoded form.
Algorithm:
1. Measure original_bytes as the UTF-8 byte length of the original text.
2. Measure encoded_length as the number of emoji symbols or encoded characters in the encoded string.
3. Compute actual_ratio as encoded_length / original_bytes, with appropriate handling for zero-length input.
4. Compute theoretical_ratio as 8.0 / bitsPerChunk, adjusted by any known codec configuration.
5. Report bits_per_emoji from the active recipe.
6. Return all statistics in a map.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- recipeType
- mask
- emojiMap
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original plain text.
- encoded: encoded emoji string.
Output:
- A map containing:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - actual_ratio
  - theoretical_ratio
  - bits_per_emoji
Pre-condition:
- original and encoded must not be null.
Post-condition:
- Returned statistics reflect the provided values and current recipe configuration.

EmojiCodec::decodeBinary
Summary:
Decodes an emoji-encoded binary payload back into a structured binary representation.
Algorithm:
1. Decode the emoji string into a JSON-compatible textual payload.
2. Parse the payload into a map containing fields content, mime_type, and size.
3. Base64-decode the content field into raw bytes.
4. Return a list containing the decoded byte array and the MIME type.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- verification
Related Classes: FileData, PreparedData
Input:
- encoded: emoji-encoded binary payload; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A list of Java objects containing:
  - raw byte array for the binary content
  - MIME type string
Pre-condition:
- encoded must not be null.
- The encoded payload must be generated by encodeBinary() or follow the expected JSON-compatible schema.
Post-condition:
- The original binary bytes and MIME type are restored for valid payloads.
- The returned structure is suitable for file writing or further processing.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary:
Applies the configured compression transform to a byte array before emoji encoding.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is "none", return the input unchanged.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the input bytes using standard zlib-compatible compression.
3. Return the transformed byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: raw byte array to process; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A byte array after compression or unchanged when compression is none.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- compressionMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- The output is suitable for subsequent chunking and emoji encoding.
- If compression is none, output equals input.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary:
Encodes binary data into an emoji string by wrapping it in a JSON-compatible structure that preserves MIME type and size.
Algorithm:
1. Build a structured payload with fields:
   - content: Base64 text of the input bytes
   - mime_type: provided MIME type
   - size: original byte length
2. Serialize the payload to text.
3. Encode the serialized text with the same mechanism used by encode().
4. Return the resulting emoji string.
Related Features:
- emojiMap
- bitsPerChunk
- compression
- verification
Related Classes: PreparedData, FileData
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type of the binary data; may be null or empty only if the caller intentionally has no known type.
- data: binary content bytes; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- Emoji string encoding the binary payload.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized.
- The binary payload must be serializable to the required JSON-compatible schema.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with decodeBinary() restores the original bytes and MIME type.
- The binary payload is preserved using the field names content, mime_type, and size.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text, optionally reversing compression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. Convert each emoji symbol to its corresponding chunk using the active reverse emoji alphabet.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble the bit stream into bytes using the current bitsPerChunk and mask.
6. If compression mode is "zlib", uncompress the byte stream.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 bytes into a text string.
8. Return the decoded text.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: emoji-encoded text; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- The decoded UTF-8 text string.
- Empty string if the input is empty.
Pre-condition:
- emojiData must not be null.
- reverseMap and related codec configuration must already be initialized.
- Every symbol in the input must belong to the active emoji alphabet.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the inverse of encode() for valid inputs.
- Invalid symbols cause rejection/failure rather than silent corruption.

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData
Summary:
Prepares binary data for emoji encoding by serializing it into a structured payload.
Algorithm:
1. Base64-encode the input byte array into a text string.
2. Create a PreparedData instance with:
   - content set to the Base64 text
   - mimeType set to the supplied MIME type
   - size set to the input byte length
3. Return the prepared structure.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type string for the data.
- data: raw bytes to be prepared; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- PreparedData containing Base64 content, MIME type, and original size.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- The MIME type and byte data must be acceptable for serialization.
Post-condition:
- The resulting PreparedData preserves the original byte length and MIME type.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData
Summary:
Restores raw bytes from a structured PreparedData object by decoding its Base64 content.
Algorithm:
1. Read content from the PreparedData object.
2. Base64-decode the content field.
3. Return the resulting byte array.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- preparedData: structured binary payload containing Base64 content, MIME type, and size.
Output:
- Raw byte array restored from the prepared payload.
Pre-condition:
- preparedData must not be null.
- preparedData.content must contain valid Base64 text.
Post-condition:
- Returned bytes match the original binary content represented by preparedData.

EmojiCodec::unprocessData
Summary:
Reverses the configured compression transform on a byte array.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is "none", return the input unchanged.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", decompress the input bytes using standard zlib-compatible decompression.
3. Return the restored byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: compressed byte array; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A byte array after decompression or unchanged when compression is none.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- compressionMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- The output is suitable for UTF-8 decoding or binary payload restoration.
- If compression is none, output equals input.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary:
Suggests an emoji recipe based on file size.
Algorithm:
1. If size is less than 1024 bytes, return quick.
2. Else if size is less than 10 * 1024 bytes, return light.
3. Else if size is less than 100 * 1024 bytes, return classic.
4. Otherwise return gourmet.
Related Features:
- recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input:
- size: file size in bytes.
Output:
- A recipe name: quick, light, classic, or gourmet.
Pre-condition:
- size must be non-negative.
Post-condition:
- Returned recipe matches the declared size thresholds.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encodes UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet, optionally compressing first.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the input text to UTF-8 bytes.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the byte stream; if "none", keep it unchanged.
3. Split the resulting byte stream into bit chunks of size bitsPerChunk.
4. Apply the current mask to each chunk and map each chunk to an emoji symbol from emojiMap.
5. Concatenate all symbols into the final emoji string.
6. For empty input text, return an empty string.
Related Features:
- recipeType
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: text to encode in UTF-8; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- Emoji string representing the input text.
- Empty string when input text is empty.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- emojiMap and codec configuration must be initialized.
- Compression setting must be one of the supported values.
Post-condition:
- The returned emoji string decodes back to the original text using decode() for valid inputs.
- The original text is not modified.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary:
Processes a file for encoding or decoding and writes the result to an output location.
Algorithm:
1. Read the input file through FileHandler.
2. Depending on operation:
   - encode: encode file bytes into emoji text or emoji-wrapped content and write output
   - decode: decode emoji text back into bytes and write output
3. Create missing parent directories for the output path when needed.
4. Return a result map containing relevant size, MIME type, and ratio information.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- compression
- verification
- bitsPerChunk
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- inputPath: path of the input file.
- outputPath: path where output should be written.
- operation: either encode or decode, determining the workflow.
Output:
- A map containing file-processing result information such as:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - mime_type
  - actual_ratio
  - or decoded_size for decode operations
Pre-condition:
- inputPath and outputPath must be valid paths.
- operation must be a supported file processing mode.
- The input file must be readable.
Post-condition:
- The output file is written successfully when no error occurs.
- Parent directories are created if missing.
- The returned map reflects the performed operation.

EmojiCodec::getFileInfo
Summary:
Retrieves file metadata, processing feasibility, and a suggested recipe based on file size.
Algorithm:
1. Read the file metadata and content through FileHandler.
2. Determine file size in bytes and MIME type.
3. Compute can_process according to internal codec/file constraints.
4. Suggest a recipe from file size:
   - below 1 KB: quick
   - below 10 KB: light
   - below 100 KB: classic
   - otherwise: gourmet
5. Return a map containing size, mime_type, can_process, suggested_recipe, or an error state with can_process false.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- suggestRecipe
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- filePath: path to the file to inspect.
Output:
- A map containing:
  - size: file size in bytes
  - mime_type: detected MIME type
  - can_process: whether the file is processable
  - suggested_recipe: a recipe name when processable
  - optionally an error description when not processable
Pre-condition:
- filePath must identify an accessible file path.
Post-condition:
- The returned map reports file metadata consistently with the file contents and recipe policy.
- If processing is not possible, can_process is false.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary:
Computes an integrity digest for the given byte array.
Algorithm:
1. If verification mode is "none", return an empty string.
2. If verification mode is "sha256", compute SHA-256 over the input bytes.
3. Convert the digest to a lowercase hexadecimal string, left-padding each byte with a leading zero when needed.
4. Return the resulting 64-character hex string.
Related Features:
- verification
- verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input:
- data: raw bytes to hash; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string when verification is enabled.
- An empty string when verification is "none".
Pre-condition:
- The input byte array must be non-null.
- verificationMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- Returned value matches the selected verification mode.
- The input data is not modified.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Summary:
Restores raw bytes from a map-based binary payload representation.
Algorithm:
1. Read the content field from the map.
2. Interpret the value as Base64 text.
3. Base64-decode the content into bytes.
4. Return the decoded byte array.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- data: map containing at least the field content, and optionally mime_type and size.
Output:
- Raw byte array restored from the map payload.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- data must contain a valid Base64-encoded content entry.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes match the content field stored in the map.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary:
Computes encoding statistics for an original text and its emoji-encoded form.
Algorithm:
1. Measure original_bytes as the UTF-8 byte length of the original text.
2. Measure encoded_length as the number of emoji symbols or encoded characters in the encoded string.
3. Compute actual_ratio as encoded_length / original_bytes, with appropriate handling for zero-length input.
4. Compute theoretical_ratio as 8.0 / bitsPerChunk, adjusted by any known codec configuration.
5. Report bits_per_emoji from the active recipe.
6. Return all statistics in a map.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- recipeType
- mask
- emojiMap
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original plain text.
- encoded: encoded emoji string.
Output:
- A map containing:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - actual_ratio
  - theoretical_ratio
  - bits_per_emoji
Pre-condition:
- original and encoded must not be null.
Post-condition:
- Returned statistics reflect the provided values and current recipe configuration.

EmojiCodec::decodeBinary
Summary:
Decodes an emoji-encoded binary payload back into a structured binary representation.
Algorithm:
1. Decode the emoji string into a JSON-compatible textual payload.
2. Parse the payload into a map containing fields content, mime_type, and size.
3. Base64-decode the content field into raw bytes.
4. Return a list containing the decoded byte array and the MIME type.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- verification
Related Classes: FileData, PreparedData
Input:
- encoded: emoji-encoded binary payload; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A list of Java objects containing:
  - raw byte array for the binary content
  - MIME type string
Pre-condition:
- encoded must not be null.
- The encoded payload must be generated by encodeBinary() or follow the expected JSON-compatible schema.
Post-condition:
- The original binary bytes and MIME type are restored for valid payloads.
- The returned structure is suitable for file writing or further processing.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary:
Applies the configured compression transform to a byte array before emoji encoding.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is "none", return the input unchanged.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the input bytes using standard zlib-compatible compression.
3. Return the transformed byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: raw byte array to process; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A byte array after compression or unchanged when compression is none.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- compressionMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- The output is suitable for subsequent chunking and emoji encoding.
- If compression is none, output equals input.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary:
Encodes binary data into an emoji string by wrapping it in a JSON-compatible structure that preserves MIME type and size.
Algorithm:
1. Build a structured payload with fields:
   - content: Base64 text of the input bytes
   - mime_type: provided MIME type
   - size: original byte length
2. Serialize the payload to text.
3. Encode the serialized text with the same mechanism used by encode().
4. Return the resulting emoji string.
Related Features:
- emojiMap
- bitsPerChunk
- compression
- verification
Related Classes: PreparedData, FileData
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type of the binary data; may be null or empty only if the caller intentionally has no known type.
- data: binary content bytes; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- Emoji string encoding the binary payload.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized.
- The binary payload must be serializable to the required JSON-compatible schema.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with decodeBinary() restores the original bytes and MIME type.
- The binary payload is preserved using the field names content, mime_type, and size.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text, optionally reversing compression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. Convert each emoji symbol to its corresponding chunk using the active reverse emoji alphabet.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble the bit stream into bytes using the current bitsPerChunk and mask.
6. If compression mode is "zlib", uncompress the byte stream.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 bytes into a text string.
8. Return the decoded text.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: emoji-encoded text; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- The decoded UTF-8 text string.
- Empty string if the input is empty.
Pre-condition:
- emojiData must not be null.
- reverseMap and related codec configuration must already be initialized.
- Every symbol in the input must belong to the active emoji alphabet.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the inverse of encode() for valid inputs.
- Invalid symbols cause rejection/failure rather than silent corruption.

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData
Summary:
Prepares binary data for emoji encoding by serializing it into a structured payload.
Algorithm:
1. Base64-encode the input byte array into a text string.
2. Create a PreparedData instance with:
   - content set to the Base64 text
   - mimeType set to the supplied MIME type
   - size set to the input byte length
3. Return the prepared structure.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type string for the data.
- data: raw bytes to be prepared; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- PreparedData containing Base64 content, MIME type, and original size.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- The MIME type and byte data must be acceptable for serialization.
Post-condition:
- The resulting PreparedData preserves the original byte length and MIME type.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData
Summary:
Restores raw bytes from a structured PreparedData object by decoding its Base64 content.
Algorithm:
1. Read content from the PreparedData object.
2. Base64-decode the content field.
3. Return the resulting byte array.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- preparedData: structured binary payload containing Base64 content, MIME type, and size.
Output:
- Raw byte array restored from the prepared payload.
Pre-condition:
- preparedData must not be null.
- preparedData.content must contain valid Base64 text.
Post-condition:
- Returned bytes match the original binary content represented by preparedData.

EmojiCodec::unprocessData
Summary:
Reverses the configured compression transform on a byte array.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is "none", return the input unchanged.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", decompress the input bytes using standard zlib-compatible decompression.
3. Return the restored byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: compressed byte array; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A byte array after decompression or unchanged when compression is none.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- compressionMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- The output is suitable for UTF-8 decoding or binary payload restoration.
- If compression is none, output equals input.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary:
Suggests an emoji recipe based on file size.
Algorithm:
1. If size is less than 1024 bytes, return quick.
2. Else if size is less than 10 * 1024 bytes, return light.
3. Else if size is less than 100 * 1024 bytes, return classic.
4. Otherwise return gourmet.
Related Features:
- recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input:
- size: file size in bytes.
Output:
- A recipe name: quick, light, classic, or gourmet.
Pre-condition:
- size must be non-negative.
Post-condition:
- Returned recipe matches the declared size thresholds.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encodes UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet, optionally compressing first.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the input text to UTF-8 bytes.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the byte stream; if "none", keep it unchanged.
3. Split the resulting byte stream into bit chunks of size bitsPerChunk.
4. Apply the current mask to each chunk and map each chunk to an emoji symbol from emojiMap.
5. Concatenate all symbols into the final emoji string.
6. For empty input text, return an empty string.
Related Features:
- recipeType
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: text to encode in UTF-8; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- Emoji string representing the input text.
- Empty string when input text is empty.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- emojiMap and codec configuration must be initialized.
- Compression setting must be one of the supported values.
Post-condition:
- The returned emoji string decodes back to the original text using decode() for valid inputs.
- The original text is not modified.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary:
Processes a file for encoding or decoding and writes the result to an output location.
Algorithm:
1. Read the input file through FileHandler.
2. Depending on operation:
   - encode: encode file bytes into emoji text or emoji-wrapped content and write output
   - decode: decode emoji text back into bytes and write output
3. Create missing parent directories for the output path when needed.
4. Return a result map containing relevant size, MIME type, and ratio information.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- compression
- verification
- bitsPerChunk
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- inputPath: path of the input file.
- outputPath: path where output should be written.
- operation: either encode or decode, determining the workflow.
Output:
- A map containing file-processing result information such as:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - mime_type
  - actual_ratio
  - or decoded_size for decode operations
Pre-condition:
- inputPath and outputPath must be valid paths.
- operation must be a supported file processing mode.
- The input file must be readable.
Post-condition:
- The output file is written successfully when no error occurs.
- Parent directories are created if missing.
- The returned map reflects the performed operation.

EmojiCodec::getFileInfo
Summary:
Retrieves file metadata, processing feasibility, and a suggested recipe based on file size.
Algorithm:
1. Read the file metadata and content through FileHandler.
2. Determine file size in bytes and MIME type.
3. Compute can_process according to internal codec/file constraints.
4. Suggest a recipe from file size:
   - below 1 KB: quick
   - below 10 KB: light
   - below 100 KB: classic
   - otherwise: gourmet
5. Return a map containing size, mime_type, can_process, suggested_recipe, or an error state with can_process false.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- suggestRecipe
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- filePath: path to the file to inspect.
Output:
- A map containing:
  - size: file size in bytes
  - mime_type: detected MIME type
  - can_process: whether the file is processable
  - suggested_recipe: a recipe name when processable
  - optionally an error description when not processable
Pre-condition:
- filePath must identify an accessible file path.
Post-condition:
- The returned map reports file metadata consistently with the file contents and recipe policy.
- If processing is not possible, can_process is false.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary:
Computes an integrity digest for the given byte array.
Algorithm:
1. If verification mode is "none", return an empty string.
2. If verification mode is "sha256", compute SHA-256 over the input bytes.
3. Convert the digest to a lowercase hexadecimal string, left-padding each byte with a leading zero when needed.
4. Return the resulting 64-character hex string.
Related Features:
- verification
- verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input:
- data: raw bytes to hash; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string when verification is enabled.
- An empty string when verification is "none".
Pre-condition:
- The input byte array must be non-null.
- verificationMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- Returned value matches the selected verification mode.
- The input data is not modified.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Summary:
Restores raw bytes from a map-based binary payload representation.
Algorithm:
1. Read the content field from the map.
2. Interpret the value as Base64 text.
3. Base64-decode the content into bytes.
4. Return the decoded byte array.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- data: map containing at least the field content, and optionally mime_type and size.
Output:
- Raw byte array restored from the map payload.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- data must contain a valid Base64-encoded content entry.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes match the content field stored in the map.

Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- recipeType
- mask
- emojiMap
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original plain text.
- encoded: encoded emoji string.
Output:
- A map containing:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - actual_ratio
  - theoretical_ratio
  - bits_per_emoji
Pre-condition:
- original and encoded must not be null.
Post-condition:
- Returned statistics reflect the provided values and current recipe configuration.

3. Return the transformed byte array.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary:
Encodes binary data into an emoji string by wrapping it in a JSON-compatible structure that preserves MIME type and size.
Algorithm:
1. Build a structured payload with fields:
   - content: Base64 text of the input bytes
   - mime_type: provided MIME type
   - size: original byte length
2. Serialize the payload to text.
3. Encode the serialized text with the same mechanism used by encode().
4. Return the resulting emoji string.
Related Features:
- emojiMap
- bitsPerChunk
- compression
- verification
Related Classes: PreparedData, FileData
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type of the binary data; may be null or empty only if the caller intentionally has no known type.
- data: binary content bytes; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- Emoji string encoding the binary payload.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized.
- The binary payload must be serializable to the required JSON-compatible schema.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with decodeBinary() restores the original bytes and MIME type.
- The binary payload is preserved using the field names content, mime_type, and size.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text, optionally reversing compression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. Convert each emoji symbol to its corresponding chunk using the active reverse emoji alphabet.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble the bit stream into bytes using the current bitsPerChunk and mask.
6. If compression mode is "zlib", uncompress the byte stream.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 bytes into a text string.
8. Return the decoded text.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: emoji-encoded text; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- The decoded UTF-8 text string.
- Empty string if the input is empty.
Pre-condition:
- emojiData must not be null.
- reverseMap and related codec configuration must already be initialized.
- Every symbol in the input must belong to the active emoji alphabet.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the inverse of encode() for valid inputs.
- Invalid symbols cause rejection/failure rather than silent corruption.

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData
Summary:
Prepares binary data for emoji encoding by serializing it into a structured payload.
Algorithm:
1. Base64-encode the input byte array into a text string.
2. Create a PreparedData instance with:
   - content set to the Base64 text
   - mimeType set to the supplied MIME type
   - size set to the input byte length
3. Return the prepared structure.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:

- data: raw bytes to be prepared; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- PreparedData containing Base64 content, MIME type, and original size.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- The MIME type and byte data must be acceptable for serialization.
Post-condition:
- The resulting PreparedData preserves the original byte length and MIME type.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData

Suggests an emoji recipe based on file size.

1. If size is less than 1024 bytes, return quick.
2. Else if size is less than 10 * 1024 bytes, return light.
3. Else if size is less than 100 * 1024 bytes, return classic.
4. Otherwise return gourmet.

- recipeType

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encodes UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet, optionally compressing first.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the input text to UTF-8 bytes.
2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the byte stream; if "none", keep it unchanged.
3. Split the resulting byte stream into bit chunks of size bitsPerChunk.
4. Apply the current mask to each chunk and map each chunk to an emoji symbol from emojiMap.
5. Concatenate all symbols into the final emoji string.
6. For empty input text, return an empty string.
Related Features:
- recipeType
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: text to encode in UTF-8; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- Emoji string representing the input text.
- Empty string when input text is empty.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- emojiMap and codec configuration must be initialized.
- Compression setting must be one of the supported values.
Post-condition:
- The returned emoji string decodes back to the original text using decode() for valid inputs.
- The original text is not modified.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary:
Processes a file for encoding or decoding and writes the result to an output location.
Algorithm:
1. Read the input file through FileHandler.
2. Depending on operation:
   - encode: encode file bytes into emoji text or emoji-wrapped content and write output
   - decode: decode emoji text back into bytes and write output
3. Create missing parent directories for the output path when needed.
4. Return a result map containing relevant size, MIME type, and ratio information.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- compression
- verification
- bitsPerChunk
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- inputPath: path of the input file.
- outputPath: path where output should be written.
- operation: either encode or decode, determining the workflow.
Output:
- A map containing file-processing result information such as:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - mime_type
  - actual_ratio
  - or decoded_size for decode operations
Pre-condition:
- inputPath and outputPath must be valid paths.
- operation must be a supported file processing mode.
- The input file must be readable.
Post-condition:
- The output file is written successfully when no error occurs.
- Parent directories are created if missing.
- The returned map reflects the performed operation.

Pre-condition:

Post-condition:

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

Summary:
Computes encoding statistics for an original text and its emoji-encoded form.
Algorithm:
1. Measure original_bytes as the UTF-8 byte length of the original text.
2. Measure encoded_length as the number of emoji symbols or encoded characters in the encoded string.
3. Compute actual_ratio as encoded_length / original_bytes, with appropriate handling for zero-length input.
4. Compute theoretical_ratio as 8.0 / bitsPerChunk, adjusted by the current recipe configuration.
5. Report bits_per_emoji from the active recipe, i.e. bitsPerChunk.
6. Return all statistics in a map.
Related Features:

- emojiMap

3. Create missing parent directories for the output path when needed.
4. Return a result map containing relevant size, MIME type, and ratio information.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- compression
- verification
- bitsPerChunk
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- inputPath: path of the input file.
- outputPath: path where output should be written.
- operation: either encode or decode, determining the workflow.
Output:
- A map containing file-processing result information such as:
  - original_bytes
  - encoded_length
  - mime_type
  - actual_ratio
  - or decoded_size for decode operations
Pre-condition:
- inputPath and outputPath must be valid paths.
- operation must be a supported file processing mode.
- The input file must be readable.
Post-condition:
- The output file is written successfully when no error occurs.
- Parent directories are created if missing.
- The returned map reflects the performed operation.

EmojiCodec::getFileInfo
Summary:
Retrieves file metadata, processing feasibility, and a suggested recipe based on file size.
Algorithm:
1. Read the file metadata and content through FileHandler.
2. Determine file size in bytes and MIME type.
3. Compute can_process according to internal codec/file constraints.
4. Suggest a recipe from file size:
   - below 1 KB: quick
   - below 10 KB: light
   - below 100 KB: classic
   - otherwise: gourmet
5. Return a map containing size, mime_type, can_process, suggested_recipe, or an error state with can_process false.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- suggestRecipe
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- filePath: path to the file to inspect.
Output:
- A map containing:
  - size: file size in bytes
  - mime_type: detected MIME type
  - can_process: whether the file is processable
  - suggested_recipe: a recipe name when processable
  - optionally an error description when not processable
Pre-condition:
- filePath must identify an accessible file path.
Post-condition:
- The returned map reports file metadata consistently with the file contents and recipe policy.
- If processing is not possible, can_process is false.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary:
Computes an integrity digest for the given byte array.
Algorithm:
1. If verification mode is "none", return an empty string.
2. If verification mode is "sha256", compute SHA-256 over the input bytes.
3. Convert the digest to a lowercase hexadecimal string, left-padding each byte with a leading zero when needed.
4. Return the resulting 64-character hex string.
Related Features:
- verification
- verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input:
- data: raw bytes to hash; may be empty but shall not be null.
Output:
- A lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string when verification is enabled.
- An empty string when verification is "none".
Pre-condition:
- The input byte array must be non-null.
- verificationMethod must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- Returned value matches the selected verification mode.
- The input data is not modified.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Summary:
Restores raw bytes from a map-based binary payload representation.
Algorithm:
1. Read the content field from the map.
2. Interpret the value as Base64 text.
3. Base64-decode the content into bytes.
4. Return the decoded byte array.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- data: map containing at least the field content, and optionally mime_type and size.
Output:
- Raw byte array restored from the map payload.
Pre-condition:
- data must not be null.
- data must contain a valid Base64-encoded content entry.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes match the content field stored in the map.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

Infers a MIME type from a file path when possible.

1. Inspect the file extension or path name.
2. Map common extensions to MIME types.

- None

- path must not be null.
Post-condition:
- Returned MIME type is never null; unknown types fall back to application/octet-stream.

Summary:

Algorithm:
1. Read all bytes from the given file path.
2. Infer the MIME type using guessMimeType(path).
3. Create and return a FileData object containing the bytes and MIME type.
Related Features:
- None

- FileData containing the file bytes and MIME type.

- MIME type is inferred from the path when possible.

- None.

- Missing parent directories are created when necessary.

   * Summary:
   * Encodes UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet, optionally compressing first.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Convert the input text to UTF-8 bytes.
   * 2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the byte stream; if "none", keep it unchanged.
   * 3. Split the resulting byte stream into bit chunks of size bitsPerChunk.
   * 4. Apply the current mask to each chunk and map each chunk to an emoji symbol from emojiMap.
   * 5. Concatenate all symbols into the final emoji string.
   * 6. For empty input text, return an empty string.
   * Related Features:
   * - recipeType
   * - bitsPerChunk
   * - mask
   * - emojiMap
   * - compression
   * - compressionMethod
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: text to encode in UTF-8; may be empty but shall not be null.
   * Output:
   * - Emoji string representing the input text.
   * - Empty string when input text is empty.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - data must not be null.
   * - emojiMap and codec configuration must be initialized.
   * - Compression setting must be one of the supported values.

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Encodes UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet, optionally compressing first.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Convert the input text to UTF-8 bytes.
   * 2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the byte stream; if "none", keep it unchanged.
   * 3. Split the resulting byte stream into bit chunks of size bitsPerChunk.
   * 4. Apply the current mask to each chunk and map each chunk to an emoji symbol from emojiMap.
   * 5. Concatenate all symbols into the final emoji string.
   * 6. For empty input text, return an empty string.
   * Related Features:
   * - recipeType
   * - bitsPerChunk
   * - mask

   * - compression
   * - compressionMethod
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: text to encode in UTF-8; may be empty but shall not be null.
   * Output:
   * - Emoji string representing the input text.
   * - Empty string when input text is empty.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - data must not be null.
   * - emojiMap and codec configuration must be initialized.
   * - Compression setting must be one of the supported values.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The returned emoji string decodes back to the original text using decode() for valid inputs.
   * - The original text is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public String encode(final String data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    if (data.isEmpty())
    {
      return "";
    }
    byte[] bytes = data.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    bytes = processData(bytes);
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    int bits = getBitsPerChunk();
    int m = getMask();
    if (bits <= 0)
    {
      throw new IllegalStateException("bitsPerChunk must be positive");
    }
    if (getEmojiMap() == null || getEmojiMap().isEmpty())
    {
      throw new IllegalStateException("emojiMap must be initialized");
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++)
    {
      int value = bytes[i] & 0xFF;
      value &= m;
      String emoji = getEmojiMap().get(Integer.valueOf(value));
      if (emoji == null)
      {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No emoji mapping for value: " + value);
      }
      result.append(emoji);
    }
    return result.toString();
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text, optionally reversing compression.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Reject null input.
   * 2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
   * 3. Convert each emoji symbol to its corresponding chunk using the active reverse emoji alphabet.
   * 4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
   * 5. Reassemble the bit stream into bytes using the current bitsPerChunk and mask.
   * 6. If compression mode is "zlib", uncompress the byte stream.
   * 7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 bytes into a text string.
   * 8. Return the decoded text.
   * Related Features:
   * - bitsPerChunk
   * - mask
   * - emojiMap
   * - reverseMap
   * - compression
   * - compressionMethod
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input:
   * - emojiData: emoji-encoded text; may be empty but shall not be null.
   * Output:
   * - The decoded UTF-8 text string.
   * - Empty string if the input is empty.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - emojiData must not be null.
   * - reverseMap and related codec configuration must already be initialized.
   * - Every symbol in the input must belong to the active emoji alphabet.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The returned text is the inverse of encode() for valid inputs.
   * - Invalid symbols cause rejection/failure rather than silent corruption.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public String decode(final String emojiData)
  {
    if (emojiData == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("emojiData must not be null");
    }
    if (emojiData.isEmpty())
    {
      return "";
    }
    if (getReverseMap() == null || getReverseMap().isEmpty())
    {
      throw new IllegalStateException("reverseMap must be initialized");
    }
    StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder();
    int index = 0;
    while (index < emojiData.length())
    {
      boolean matched = false;
      for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry : getReverseMap().entrySet())
      {
        String emoji = entry.getKey();
        if (emojiData.startsWith(emoji, index))
        {
          int value = entry.getValue().intValue() & getMask();
          text.append((char) value);
          index += emoji.length();
          matched = true;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (!matched)
      {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid emoji symbol at index " + index);
      }
    }
    byte[] bytes = text.toString().getBytes(StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1);
    bytes = unprocessData(bytes);
    return new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Computes encoding statistics for an original text and its emoji-encoded form.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Measure original_bytes as the UTF-8 byte length of the original text.
   * 2. Measure encoded_length as the number of emoji symbols or encoded characters in the encoded string.
   * 3. Compute actual_ratio as encoded_length / original_bytes, with appropriate handling for zero-length input.
   * 4. Compute theoretical_ratio as 8.0 / bitsPerChunk, adjusted by the current recipe configuration.
   * 5. Report bits_per_emoji from the active recipe, i.e. bitsPerChunk.
   * 6. Return all statistics in a map.
   * Related Features:
   * - bitsPerChunk
   * - recipeType
   * - mask
   * - emojiMap
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input:
   * - original: original plain text.
   * - encoded: encoded emoji string.
   * Output:
   * - A map containing:
   *   - original_bytes
   *   - encoded_length
   *   - actual_ratio
   *   - theoretical_ratio
   *   - bits_per_emoji
   * Pre-condition:
   * - original and encoded must not be null.
   * Post-condition:
   * - Returned statistics reflect the provided values and current recipe configuration.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, Double> getStats(final String original, final String encoded)
  {
    if (original == null || encoded == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("original and encoded must not be null");
    }
    Map<String, Double> stats = new HashMap<String, Double>();
    int originalBytes = original.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length;
    int encodedLength = encoded.isEmpty() ? 0 : encoded.length();
    double actualRatio = originalBytes == 0 ? 0.0 : ((double) encodedLength) / originalBytes;
    double theoreticalRatio = getBitsPerChunk() <= 0 ? 0.0 : 8.0 / getBitsPerChunk();
    stats.put("original_bytes", Double.valueOf(originalBytes));
    stats.put("encoded_length", Double.valueOf(encodedLength));
    stats.put("actual_ratio", Double.valueOf(actualRatio));
    stats.put("theoretical_ratio", Double.valueOf(theoreticalRatio));
    stats.put("bits_per_emoji", Double.valueOf(getBitsPerChunk()));
    return stats;
    
  }

  public EList<Object> decodeBinary(final String encoded)
  {
    if (encoded == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("encoded must not be null");
    }
    EList<Object> result = new BasicEList<Object>();
    if (encoded.isEmpty())
    {
      return result;
    }
    String payload = decode(encoded);
    String content = extractJsonString(payload, "content");
    String mimeType = extractJsonString(payload, "mime_type");

    result.add(bytes);
    result.add(mimeType);
    return result;
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Processes a file for encoding or decoding and writes the result to an output location.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Read the input file through FileHandler.
   * 2. Depending on operation:
   *    - encode: encode file bytes into emoji text or emoji-wrapped content and write output
   *    - decode: decode emoji text back into bytes and write output
   * 3. Create missing parent directories for the output path when needed.
   * 4. Return a result map containing relevant size, MIME type, and ratio information.
   * Related Features:
   * - fileHandler

   * - verification

   * Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
   * Input:
   * - inputPath: path of the input file.
   * - outputPath: path where output should be written.
   * - operation: either encode or decode, determining the workflow.
   * Output:
   * - A map containing file-processing result information such as:
   *   - original_bytes
   *   - encoded_length
   *   - mime_type
   *   - actual_ratio
   *   - or decoded_size for decode operations
   * Pre-condition:
   * - inputPath and outputPath must be valid paths.
   * - operation must be a supported file processing mode.
   * - The input file must be readable.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The output file is written successfully when no error occurs.
   * - Parent directories are created if missing.
   * - The returned map reflects the performed operation.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, Object> processFile(final String inputPath, final String outputPath, final String operation)
  {
    if (inputPath == null || outputPath == null || operation == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("inputPath, outputPath, and operation must not be null");
    }
    Map<String, Object> result = new HashMap<String, Object>();
    FileData fileData = getFileHandler().readFile(inputPath);
    java.nio.file.Path out = java.nio.file.Paths.get(outputPath);
    java.nio.file.Path parent = out.getParent();
    if (parent != null)
    {
      try
      {
        java.nio.file.Files.createDirectories(parent);
      }
      catch (IOException e)
      {
        throw new RuntimeException(e);
      }
    }
    if ("encode".equalsIgnoreCase(operation))
    {
      String encoded = encodeBinary(fileData.getMimeType(), fileData.getContent());
      getFileHandler().writeFile(outputPath, encoded.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
      result.put("original_bytes", Double.valueOf(fileData.getContent().length));
      result.put("encoded_length", Double.valueOf(encoded.length()));
      result.put("mime_type", fileData.getMimeType());
      result.put("actual_ratio", Double.valueOf(fileData.getContent().length == 0 ? 0.0 : ((double) encoded.length()) / fileData.getContent().length));
    }
    else if ("decode".equalsIgnoreCase(operation))
    {
      String encoded = new String(fileData.getContent(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
      EList<Object> decoded = decodeBinary(encoded);
      byte[] bytes = (byte[]) decoded.get(0);
      getFileHandler().writeFile(outputPath, bytes);
      result.put("decoded_size", Double.valueOf(bytes.length));
      result.put("mime_type", decoded.size() > 1 ? decoded.get(1) : null);
    }
    else
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unsupported operation: " + operation);
    }
    return result;
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Applies the configured compression transform to a byte array before emoji encoding.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If compression mode is "none", return the input unchanged.
   * 2. If compression mode is "zlib", compress the input bytes using standard zlib-compatible compression.
   * 3. Return the transformed byte array.
   * Related Features:
   * - compression
   * - compressionMethod
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: raw byte array to process; may be empty but shall not be null.
   * Output:
   * - A byte array after compression or unchanged when compression is none.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - data must not be null.
   * - compressionMethod must be initialized.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The output is suitable for subsequent chunking and emoji encoding.
   * - If compression is none, output equals input.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public byte[] processData(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    String mode = getCompression();
    if (mode == null || "none".equalsIgnoreCase(mode))
    {
      return data;
    }
    if (!"zlib".equalsIgnoreCase(mode))
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unsupported compression mode: " + mode);
    }
    try
    {
      ByteArrayOutputStream baos = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
      try (DeflaterOutputStream dos = new DeflaterOutputStream(baos))
      {
        dos.write(data);
      }
      return baos.toByteArray();
    }
    catch (IOException e)
    {
      throw new RuntimeException(e);
    }
    
  }

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Reverses the configured compression transform on a byte array.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If compression mode is "none", return the input unchanged.
   * 2. If compression mode is "zlib", decompress the input bytes using standard zlib-compatible decompression.
   * 3. Return the restored byte array.

  public byte[] unprocessData(final byte[] data)

    {

      try (InflaterOutputStream ios = new InflaterOutputStream(baos))
      {
        ios.write(data);
      }
      return baos.toByteArray();
    }
    catch (IOException e)
    {
      throw new RuntimeException(e);
    }
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Computes an integrity digest for the given byte array.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If verification mode is "none", return an empty string.
   * 2. If verification mode is "sha256", compute SHA-256 over the input bytes.
   * 3. Convert the digest to a lowercase hexadecimal string, left-padding each byte with a leading zero when needed.
   * 4. Return the resulting 64-character hex string.
   * Related Features:
   * - verification
   * - verificationMethod
   * Related Classes: VerificationMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: raw bytes to hash; may be empty but shall not be null.
   * Output:
   * - A lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string when verification is enabled.
   * - An empty string when verification is "none".
   * Pre-condition:
   * - The input byte array must be non-null.
   * - verificationMethod must be initialized.
   * Post-condition:
   * - Returned value matches the selected verification mode.
   * - The input data is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public String calculateHash(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    String mode = getVerification();
    if (mode == null || "none".equalsIgnoreCase(mode))
    {
      return "";
    }
    if (!"sha256".equalsIgnoreCase(mode))
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unsupported verification mode: " + mode);
    }
    try
    {
      MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
      byte[] hash = digest.digest(data);
      StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
      for (byte b : hash)
      {
        String hex = Integer.toHexString(b & 0xFF);
        if (hex.length() == 1)
        {
          sb.append('0');
        }
        sb.append(hex);
      }
      return sb.toString();
    }
    catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException e)
    {
      throw new RuntimeException(e);
    }
    
  }

      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    Object content = data.get("content");
    if (content == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must contain content");
    }
    return Base64.getDecoder().decode(String.valueOf(content));
    
  }

   * Summary:
   * Suggests an emoji recipe based on file size.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If size is less than 1024 bytes, return quick.
   * 2. Else if size is less than 10 * 1024 bytes, return light.
   * 3. Else if size is less than 100 * 1024 bytes, return classic.
   * 4. Otherwise return gourmet.
   * Related Features:
   * - recipeType
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input:
   * - size: file size in bytes.
   * Output:
   * - A recipe name: quick, light, classic, or gourmet.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - size must be non-negative.
   * Post-condition:
   * - Returned recipe matches the declared size thresholds.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public String suggestRecipe(final int size)
  {
    if (size < 1024)
    {
      return "quick";
    }
    if (size < 10 * 1024)
    {
      return "light";
    }
    if (size < 100 * 1024)
    {
      return "classic";
    }
    return "gourmet";
    
  }

   *   - raw byte array for the binary content
   *   - MIME type string
   * Pre-condition:
   * - encoded must not be null.
   * - The encoded payload must be generated by encodeBinary() or follow the expected JSON-compatible schema.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The original binary bytes and MIME type are restored for valid payloads.
   * - The returned structure is suitable for file writing or further processing.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Object> decodeBinary(final String encoded)
  {
    if (encoded == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("encoded must not be null");
    }
    EList<Object> result = new BasicEList<Object>();
    if (encoded.isEmpty())
    {
      return result;
    }
    String payload = decode(encoded);
    String content = extractJsonString(payload, "content");
    String mimeType = extractJsonString(payload, "mime_type");
    byte[] bytes = Base64.getDecoder().decode(content);
    result.add(bytes);
    result.add(mimeType);
    return result;
    
  }
