```java
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='manual'"
   * @generated
   */
  public EList<Map<String, Object>> batchProcess(final String filePattern, final String outputDir, final String operation)
  {
      try {
            Path outDir = Path.of(outputDir);
            Files.createDirectories(outDir);
    
            Path patternPath = Path.of(filePattern);
            Path directory = patternPath.getParent();
    
            if (directory == null) {
                directory = Path.of(".");
            }
    
            String glob = patternPath.getFileName().toString();
    
            PathMatcher matcher = directory
                .getFileSystem()
                .getPathMatcher("glob:" + glob);
    
            BasicEList<Path> files = new BasicEList<Path>();
    
            try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream =
                    Files.newDirectoryStream(directory)) {
    
                for (Path entry : stream) {
                    if (Files.isRegularFile(entry)
                            && matcher.matches(entry.getFileName())) {
                        files.add(entry);
                    }
                }
            }
    
            BasicEList<Map<String, Object>> results =
                new BasicEList<Map<String, Object>>();
    
            for (Path inputFile : files) {
                String stem = inputFile.getFileName().toString();
                int dotIndex = stem.lastIndexOf('.');
    
                if (dotIndex > 0) {
                    stem = stem.substring(0, dotIndex);
                }
    
                Path outputPath;
    
                if ("encode".equals(operation)) {
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(stem + ".emoji");
                } else {
                    String mimeType =
                        URLConnection.guessContentTypeFromName(
                            inputFile.getFileName().toString()
                        );
    
                    String extension =
                        mimeType != null ? ".bin" : ".bin";
    
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(
                        "decoded_" + stem + extension
                    );
                }
    
                try {
                    Map<String, Object> statistics = processFile(
                        inputFile.toString(),
                        outputPath.toString(),
                        operation
                    );
    
                    statistics.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    statistics.put("success", Boolean.TRUE);
    
                    results.add(statistics);
                } catch (Exception exception) {
                    Map<String, Object> errorResult =
                        new LinkedHashMap<String, Object>();
    
                    errorResult.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    errorResult.put("success", Boolean.FALSE);
                    errorResult.put("error", exception.getMessage());
    
                    results.add(errorResult);
                }
            }
    
            return results;
        } catch (IOException exception) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Batch processing error: " + exception.getMessage(),
                exception
            );
```
```java
        }
  }

            Path patternPath = Path.of(filePattern);
            Path directory = patternPath.getParent();
    
            if (directory == null) {
                directory = Path.of(".");

            String glob = patternPath.getFileName().toString();
    
            PathMatcher matcher = directory

            BasicEList<Path> files = new BasicEList<Path>();
    
            try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream =
                    Files.newDirectoryStream(directory)) {
    
                for (Path entry : stream) {
                    if (Files.isRegularFile(entry)
                            && matcher.matches(entry.getFileName())) {
                        files.add(entry);
                    }
                }
            }
    
            BasicEList<Map<String, Object>> results =
                new BasicEList<Map<String, Object>>();
    
            for (Path inputFile : files) {
                String stem = inputFile.getFileName().toString();
                int dotIndex = stem.lastIndexOf('.');
    
                if (dotIndex > 0) {
                    stem = stem.substring(0, dotIndex);
                }
    
                Path outputPath;
    
                if ("encode".equals(operation)) {

                    String extension =

                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(

                    Map<String, Object> statistics = processFile(

                    results.add(errorResult);
                }
            }
    
            return results;

                "Batch processing error: " + exception.getMessage(),
```

            Path outDir = Path.of(outputDir);

            Path patternPath = Path.of(filePattern);
            Path directory = patternPath.getParent();
    
            if (directory == null) {
                directory = Path.of(".");
            }
    
            String glob = patternPath.getFileName().toString();
    
            PathMatcher matcher = directory
                .getFileSystem()
                .getPathMatcher("glob:" + glob);
    
            BasicEList<Path> files = new BasicEList<Path>();
    
            try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream =
                    Files.newDirectoryStream(directory)) {
    
                for (Path entry : stream) {
                    if (Files.isRegularFile(entry)
                            && matcher.matches(entry.getFileName())) {
                        files.add(entry);
                    }
                }
            }
    
            BasicEList<Map<String, Object>> results =
                new BasicEList<Map<String, Object>>();
    
            for (Path inputFile : files) {
                String stem = inputFile.getFileName().toString();
                int dotIndex = stem.lastIndexOf('.');
    
                if (dotIndex > 0) {
                    stem = stem.substring(0, dotIndex);
                }
    
                Path outputPath;
    
                if ("encode".equals(operation)) {
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(stem + ".emoji");
                } else {
                    String mimeType =
                        URLConnection.guessContentTypeFromName(
                            inputFile.getFileName().toString()
                        );
    
                    String extension =
                        mimeType != null ? ".bin" : ".bin";
    
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(
                        "decoded_" + stem + extension
                    );
                }

                    Map<String, Object> statistics = processFile(
                        inputFile.toString(),
                        outputPath.toString(),
                        operation

                    statistics.put("success", Boolean.TRUE);

                    Map<String, Object> errorResult =
                        new LinkedHashMap<String, Object>();
    
                    errorResult.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    errorResult.put("success", Boolean.FALSE);
                    errorResult.put("error", exception.getMessage());
    
                    results.add(errorResult);
                }
            }
    
            return results;
        } catch (IOException exception) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Batch processing error: " + exception.getMessage(),
                exception
            );
```plantuml
        }

                }
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.
```

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary:
Compute encoding statistics for a text payload and its emoji-encoded representation.
Algorithm:
1. Measure the original byte length of the input text using UTF-8 encoding.
2. Measure the length of the encoded emoji string.
3. Compute actual ratio = encoded_length / original_bytes, handling zero-length input safely.
4. Compute theoretical ratio based on `bitsPerChunk` and emoji symbol width assumptions used by the codec.
5. Report `bits_per_emoji` as the active chunk size in bits.
6. Return all values in a map.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- baseSize
- getStats
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original text string.
- encoded: emoji-encoded string.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` with keys:
  - `original_bytes`
  - `encoded_length`
  - `actual_ratio`
  - `theoretical_ratio`
  - `bits_per_emoji`
Pre-condition:
- Neither input may be null.
Post-condition:
- The result numerically describes the provided inputs and active recipe configuration.
- No codec state is modified.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encode UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet and optional compression.
Algorithm:
1. If the input text is empty, return an empty string.
2. Convert the text to UTF-8 bytes.
3. Process the bytes according to the configured compression mode.
4. Split the resulting byte stream into chunks of `bitsPerChunk` bits.
5. For each chunk, apply the mask and map the value to the corresponding emoji symbol.
6. Concatenate all emoji symbols into the output string.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- processData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: input text string.
- Encoded as UTF-8 before processing.
Output:
- Returns an emoji string representing the input text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- The input text must not be null.
- The emoji map must be initialized for the active recipe.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with the same codec configuration yields the original text.
- No state of the codec is modified except transient local processing.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decode an emoji string back into its original text, reversing chunk mapping and optional decompression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. For each emoji symbol in the string, look up its chunk value in the reverse emoji map.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble bit chunks into a byte array according to the active recipe size.
6. Unprocess the byte array using the configured compression mode.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 byte array to a text string and return it.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- unprocessData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: encoded emoji string.
- Must consist only of emoji symbols from the currently active recipe alphabet.
Output:
- Returns the decoded UTF-8 text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- `emojiData` must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized with emoji and reverse maps.
- Every symbol in `emojiData` must exist in the reverse map.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the original text used in encoding, if the input is valid.
- Invalid input symbols cause rejection/failure.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary:
Suggest an emoji recipe name based on file size thresholds.
Algorithm:
1. If size is less than 1 KB, return `quick`.
2. Else if size is less than 10 KB, return `light`.
3. Else if size is less than 100 KB, return `classic`.
4. Otherwise return `gourmet`.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- size: file size in bytes.
- Must be interpreted as a non-negative integer.
Output:
- Returns one of: `quick`, `light`, `classic`, `gourmet`.
Pre-condition:
- `size` must be greater than or equal to 0.
Post-condition:
- The suggested recipe corresponds to the configured thresholds.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary:
Compute encoding statistics for a text payload and its emoji-encoded representation.
Algorithm:
1. Measure the original byte length of the input text using UTF-8 encoding.
2. Measure the length of the encoded emoji string.
3. Compute actual ratio = encoded_length / original_bytes, handling zero-length input safely.
4. Compute theoretical ratio based on `bitsPerChunk` and emoji symbol width assumptions used by the codec.
5. Report `bits_per_emoji` as the active chunk size in bits.
6. Return all values in a map.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- baseSize
- getStats
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original text string.
- encoded: emoji-encoded string.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` with keys:
  - `original_bytes`
  - `encoded_length`
  - `actual_ratio`
  - `theoretical_ratio`
  - `bits_per_emoji`
Pre-condition:
- Neither input may be null.
Post-condition:
- The result numerically describes the provided inputs and active recipe configuration.
- No codec state is modified.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encode UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet and optional compression.
Algorithm:
1. If the input text is empty, return an empty string.
2. Convert the text to UTF-8 bytes.
3. Process the bytes according to the configured compression mode.
4. Split the resulting byte stream into chunks of `bitsPerChunk` bits.
5. For each chunk, apply the mask and map the value to the corresponding emoji symbol.
6. Concatenate all emoji symbols into the output string.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- processData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: input text string.
- Encoded as UTF-8 before processing.
Output:
- Returns an emoji string representing the input text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- The input text must not be null.
- The emoji map must be initialized for the active recipe.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with the same codec configuration yields the original text.
- No state of the codec is modified except transient local processing.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decode an emoji string back into its original text, reversing chunk mapping and optional decompression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. For each emoji symbol in the string, look up its chunk value in the reverse emoji map.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble bit chunks into a byte array according to the active recipe size.
6. Unprocess the byte array using the configured compression mode.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 byte array to a text string and return it.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- unprocessData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: encoded emoji string.
- Must consist only of emoji symbols from the currently active recipe alphabet.
Output:
- Returns the decoded UTF-8 text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- `emojiData` must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized with emoji and reverse maps.
- Every symbol in `emojiData` must exist in the reverse map.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the original text used in encoding, if the input is valid.
- Invalid input symbols cause rejection/failure.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary:
Suggest an emoji recipe name based on file size thresholds.
Algorithm:
1. If size is less than 1 KB, return `quick`.
2. Else if size is less than 10 KB, return `light`.
3. Else if size is less than 100 KB, return `classic`.
4. Otherwise return `gourmet`.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- size: file size in bytes.
- Must be interpreted as a non-negative integer.
Output:
- Returns one of: `quick`, `light`, `classic`, `gourmet`.
Pre-condition:
- `size` must be greater than or equal to 0.
Post-condition:
- The suggested recipe corresponds to the configured thresholds.

Algorithm:

2. If compression mode is `zlib`, compress the input using standard zlib-compatible compression.
3. Return the processed byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:

Output:

Pre-condition:
- `data` must not be null.
- The compression mode must be one of the supported methods.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes are safe to feed into emoji chunk encoding.
- The original input is not modified.

Perform a file-oriented encode or decode workflow and optionally write output to a path.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary:
Calculate a SHA-256 hash digest for the given binary data and return it as a lowercase hexadecimal string.
Algorithm:
1. If verification mode is `none`, return an empty string.
2. Otherwise, compute SHA-256 over the input byte array.
3. Convert each digest byte to a two-character lowercase hexadecimal representation with zero padding.
4. Concatenate all hex pairs and return the resulting 64-character string.
Related Features:
- verification
- verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input:
- data: binary content to hash, as `EByteArray`.
- If data is empty, the hash is still computed over an empty byte sequence.
Output:
- Returns a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string.
- Returns `""` when verification is disabled (`none`).
Pre-condition:
- The input byte array must not be null.
- The codec must have a valid verification mode configured.
Post-condition:
- The returned string is deterministic for the same input data.
- No state of the codec is modified.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary:
Compute encoding statistics for a text payload and its emoji-encoded representation.
Algorithm:
1. Measure the original byte length of the input text using UTF-8 encoding.
2. Measure the length of the encoded emoji string.
3. Compute actual ratio = encoded_length / original_bytes, handling zero-length input safely.
4. Compute theoretical ratio based on the active recipe configuration and `bitsPerChunk`.
5. Report `bits_per_emoji` as the number of bits encoded by each emoji in the active recipe.
6. Return all values in a map.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- baseSize
- getStats
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original text string.
- encoded: emoji-encoded string.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` with keys:
  - `original_bytes`
  - `encoded_length`
  - `actual_ratio`
  - `theoretical_ratio`
  - `bits_per_emoji`
Pre-condition:
- Neither input may be null.
Post-condition:
- The result numerically describes the provided inputs and active recipe configuration.
- No codec state is modified.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encode UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet and optional compression.
Algorithm:
1. If the input text is empty, return an empty string.
2. Convert the text to UTF-8 bytes.
3. Process the bytes according to the configured compression mode.
4. Split the resulting byte stream into chunks of `bitsPerChunk` bits.
5. For each chunk, apply the mask and map the value to the corresponding emoji symbol.
6. Concatenate all emoji symbols into the output string.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- processData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: input text string.
- Encoded as UTF-8 before processing.
Output:
- Returns an emoji string representing the input text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- The input text must not be null.
- The emoji map must be initialized for the active recipe.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with the same codec configuration yields the original text.
- No state of the codec is modified except transient local processing.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decode an emoji string back into its original text, reversing chunk mapping and optional decompression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. For each emoji symbol in the string, look up its chunk value in the reverse emoji map.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble bit chunks into a byte array according to the active recipe size.
6. Unprocess the byte array using the configured compression mode.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 byte array to a text string and return it.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- unprocessData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: encoded emoji string.
- Must consist only of emoji symbols from the currently active recipe alphabet.
Output:
- Returns the decoded UTF-8 text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- `emojiData` must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized with emoji and reverse maps.
- Every symbol in `emojiData` must exist in the reverse map.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the original text used in encoding, if the input is valid.
- Invalid input symbols cause rejection/failure.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary:
Suggest an emoji recipe name based on file size thresholds.
Algorithm:
1. If size is less than 1 KB, return `quick`.
2. Else if size is less than 10 KB, return `light`.
3. Else if size is less than 100 KB, return `classic`.
4. Otherwise return `gourmet`.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- size: file size in bytes.
- Must be interpreted as a non-negative integer.
Output:
- Returns one of: `quick`, `light`, `classic`, `gourmet`.
Pre-condition:
- `size` must be greater than or equal to 0.
Post-condition:
- The suggested recipe corresponds to the configured thresholds.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary:
Apply the configured compression transform to a byte array before emoji chunk mapping.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is `none`, return the input bytes unchanged.
2. If compression mode is `zlib`, compress the input using standard zlib-compatible compression.
3. Return the processed byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: byte array to process.
Output:
- Returns compressed bytes when `zlib` is selected, otherwise the original bytes.
Pre-condition:
- `data` must not be null.
- The compression mode must be one of the supported methods.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes are safe to feed into emoji chunk encoding.
- The original input is not modified.

Perform a file-oriented encode or decode workflow and optionally write output to a path.

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData

Prepare binary data for emoji encoding by converting it into a JSON-compatible structure with Base64 content.

1. Base64-encode the raw byte array.
2. Record the MIME type as provided.

Post-condition:
- The returned object preserves the MIME type and original byte length.
- The content field contains Base64 text suitable for JSON serialization.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary:
Calculate a SHA-256 hash digest for the given binary data and return it as a lowercase hexadecimal string.
Algorithm:
1. If verification mode is `none`, return an empty string.
2. Otherwise, compute SHA-256 over the input byte array.
3. Convert each digest byte to a two-character lowercase hexadecimal representation with zero padding.
4. Concatenate all hex pairs and return the resulting 64-character string.
Related Features:
- verification
- verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input:
- data: binary content to hash, as `EByteArray`.
- If data is empty, the hash is still computed over an empty byte sequence.
Output:
- Returns a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string.
- Returns `""` when verification is disabled (`none`).
Pre-condition:
- The input byte array must not be null.
- The codec must have a valid verification mode configured.
Post-condition:
- The returned string is deterministic for the same input data.
- No state of the codec is modified.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary:
Encode raw binary data with MIME metadata into an emoji string via a JSON-compatible wrapper.
Algorithm:
1. Wrap the input bytes and MIME type into a prepared structure containing Base64 content, MIME type, and size.
2. Serialize the structure into a JSON-compatible string or byte representation.
3. Treat the serialized payload as bytes and process it with the configured compression mode.
4. Convert processed bytes into emoji chunks using the active recipe alphabet.
5. Concatenate the mapped emoji symbols and return the result.
Related Features:
- prepareBinaryData
- processData
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
Related Classes: PreparedData, CompressionMethod
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type of the binary content.

Output:
- Returns an emoji string encoding the binary payload and its metadata.
Pre-condition:
- `mimeType` and `data` must not be null.
- The emoji map must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- The encoded output can be restored to the original bytes and MIME type using binary decode.
- The original size is preserved in the wrapped metadata.

EmojiCodec::decodeBinary
Summary:
Decode an emoji string that represents an encoded binary payload and restore the binary structure fields.

Pre-condition:

- The input must be a valid emoji-encoded binary payload.
Post-condition:

- No codec state is mutated.

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary:
Compute encoding statistics for a text payload and its emoji-encoded representation.
Algorithm:
1. Measure the original byte length of the input text using UTF-8 encoding.
2. Measure the length of the encoded emoji string.
3. Compute actual ratio = encoded_length / original_bytes, handling zero-length input safely.
4. Compute theoretical ratio based on the active recipe configuration and `bitsPerChunk`.
5. Report `bits_per_emoji` as the number of bits encoded by each emoji in the active recipe.
6. Return all values in a map.
Related Features:
- bitsPerChunk
- baseSize
- getStats
Related Classes: None
Input:
- original: original text string.
- encoded: emoji-encoded string.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` with keys:
  - `original_bytes`
  - `encoded_length`
  - `actual_ratio`
  - `theoretical_ratio`
  - `bits_per_emoji`
Pre-condition:
- Neither input may be null.
Post-condition:
- The result numerically describes the provided inputs and active recipe configuration.
- No codec state is modified.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary:
Encode UTF-8 text into an emoji string using the active recipe alphabet and optional compression.
Algorithm:
1. If the input text is empty, return an empty string.
2. Convert the text to UTF-8 bytes.
3. Process the bytes according to the configured compression mode.
4. Split the resulting byte stream into chunks of `bitsPerChunk` bits.
5. For each chunk, apply the mask and map the value to the corresponding emoji symbol.
6. Concatenate all emoji symbols into the output string.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- processData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: input text string.
- Encoded as UTF-8 before processing.
Output:
- Returns an emoji string representing the input text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- The input text must not be null.
- The emoji map must be initialized for the active recipe.
Post-condition:
- Decoding the returned emoji string with the same codec configuration yields the original text.
- No state of the codec is modified except transient local processing.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary:
Decode an emoji string back into its original text, reversing chunk mapping and optional decompression.
Algorithm:
1. Reject null input.
2. If the input is empty, return an empty string.
3. For each emoji symbol in the string, look up its chunk value in the reverse emoji map.
4. Reject any symbol not present in the active alphabet.
5. Reassemble bit chunks into a byte array according to the active recipe size.
6. Unprocess the byte array using the configured compression mode.
7. Convert the resulting UTF-8 byte array to a text string and return it.
Related Features:
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- reverseMap
- compression
- compressionMethod
- unprocessData
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- emojiData: encoded emoji string.
- Must consist only of emoji symbols from the currently active recipe alphabet.
Output:
- Returns the decoded UTF-8 text.
- Returns `""` for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- `emojiData` must not be null.
- The codec must be initialized with emoji and reverse maps.
- Every symbol in `emojiData` must exist in the reverse map.
Post-condition:
- The returned text is the original text used in encoding, if the input is valid.
- Invalid input symbols cause rejection/failure.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary:
Suggest an emoji recipe name based on file size thresholds.
Algorithm:
1. If size is less than 1 KB, return `quick`.
2. Else if size is less than 10 KB, return `light`.
3. Else if size is less than 100 KB, return `classic`.
4. Otherwise return `gourmet`.
Related Features:
- None
Related Classes: None
Input:
- size: file size in bytes.
- Must be interpreted as a non-negative integer.
Output:
- Returns one of: `quick`, `light`, `classic`, `gourmet`.
Pre-condition:
- `size` must be greater than or equal to 0.
Post-condition:
- The suggested recipe corresponds to the configured thresholds.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary:
Apply the configured compression transform to a byte array before emoji chunk mapping.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is `none`, return the input bytes unchanged.
2. If compression mode is `zlib`, compress the input using standard zlib-compatible compression.
3. Return the processed byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: byte array to process.
Output:
- Returns compressed bytes when `zlib` is selected, otherwise the original bytes.
Pre-condition:
- `data` must not be null.
- The compression mode must be one of the supported methods.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes are safe to feed into emoji chunk encoding.
- The original input is not modified.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary:
Perform a file-oriented encode or decode workflow and optionally write output to a path.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the requested operation (`encode` or `decode`).
2. Read the input file content through the file handler.
3. For encoding, convert file bytes to an emoji string; for decoding, convert emoji content back to bytes.
4. If an output path is provided, write the transformed bytes to the target file, creating missing parent directories.
5. Return a map containing workflow results and metadata such as byte counts and MIME type.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- encodeBinary
- decodeBinary
- suggestRecipe
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData, PreparedData
Input:
- inputPath: source file path.
- outputPath: destination file path.
- operation: workflow selector, typically `encode` or `decode`.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` describing the file processing result, including relevant sizes and MIME type.
Pre-condition:
- `inputPath` must not be null.
- `operation` must be a supported workflow keyword.
- If writing output, `outputPath` must be valid or writable.
Post-condition:
- The specified file workflow is completed or an error result is returned.
- Output files are written only when requested and feasible.

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData
Summary:
Prepare binary data for emoji encoding by converting it into a JSON-compatible structure with Base64 content.
Algorithm:
1. Base64-encode the raw byte array.
2. Record the MIME type as provided.
3. Record the original byte size.
4. Create a `PreparedData` instance with fields `content`, `mimeType`, and `size`.
5. Return the prepared structure.
Related Features:
- prepareBinaryData
- encodeBinary
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type of the binary content.
- data: raw bytes to be wrapped.
Output:
- Returns a `PreparedData` object containing Base64 content, MIME type, and original size.
Pre-condition:
- `mimeType` and `data` must not be null.
Post-condition:
- The returned object preserves the MIME type and original byte length.
- The content field contains Base64 text suitable for JSON serialization.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary:
Calculate a SHA-256 hash digest for the given binary data and return it as a lowercase hexadecimal string.
Algorithm:
1. If verification mode is `none`, return an empty string.
2. Otherwise, compute SHA-256 over the input byte array.
3. Convert each digest byte to a two-character lowercase hexadecimal representation with zero padding.
4. Concatenate all hex pairs and return the resulting 64-character string.
Related Features:
- verification
- verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input:
- data: binary content to hash, as `EByteArray`.
- If data is empty, the hash is still computed over an empty byte sequence.
Output:
- Returns a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string.
- Returns `""` when verification is disabled (`none`).
Pre-condition:
- The input byte array must not be null.
- The codec must have a valid verification mode configured.
Post-condition:
- The returned string is deterministic for the same input data.
- No state of the codec is modified.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary:
Encode raw binary data with MIME metadata into an emoji string via a JSON-compatible wrapper.
Algorithm:
1. Wrap the input bytes and MIME type into a prepared structure containing Base64 content, MIME type, and size.
2. Serialize the structure into a JSON-compatible string or byte representation.
3. Treat the serialized payload as bytes and process it with the configured compression mode.
4. Convert processed bytes into emoji chunks using the active recipe alphabet.
5. Concatenate the mapped emoji symbols and return the result.
Related Features:
- prepareBinaryData
- processData
- baseSize
- bitsPerChunk
- mask
- emojiMap
- compression
Related Classes: PreparedData, CompressionMethod
Input:
- mimeType: MIME type of the binary content.
- data: raw byte array to encode.
Output:
- Returns an emoji string encoding the binary payload and its metadata.
Pre-condition:
- `mimeType` and `data` must not be null.
- The emoji map must be initialized.
Post-condition:
- The encoded output can be restored to the original bytes and MIME type using binary decode.
- The original size is preserved in the wrapped metadata.

EmojiCodec::decodeBinary
Summary:
Decode an emoji string that represents an encoded binary payload and restore the binary structure fields.
Algorithm:
1. Decode the emoji string into the encoded JSON-compatible byte sequence.
2. Parse the decoded content into structured fields.
3. Extract `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`.
4. Base64-decode `content` to recover the original byte array.
5. Return the restored binary bytes and MIME type as specified by the implementation contract.
Related Features:
- decode
- restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- encoded: emoji-encoded binary payload.
- Expected to be produced by `encodeBinary`.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` containing the restored binary data and metadata, including:
  - `content`
  - `mime_type`
  - `size`
- The decoded result must include the original byte array and MIME type.
Pre-condition:
- `encoded` must not be null.
- The input must be a valid emoji-encoded binary payload.
Post-condition:
- The original binary content and MIME type can be reconstructed from the result.
- No codec state is mutated.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData
Summary:
Restore raw bytes from a prepared binary data structure by Base64-decoding the content field.
Algorithm:
1. Read the `content` field from the prepared data.
2. Base64-decode the content back into raw bytes.
3. Ignore or preserve metadata fields as required by the calling workflow.
4. Return the restored byte array.
Related Features:
- restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- preparedData: prepared binary payload containing Base64 content.
Output:
- Returns the raw byte array represented by the Base64 `content`.
Pre-condition:
- `preparedData` must not be null.
- `preparedData.content` must contain valid Base64 text.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes match the original input bytes used to create the prepared structure.

EmojiCodec::getFileInfo
Summary:
Retrieve file metadata and processability information for a file path, including a suggested recipe based on size.
Algorithm:
1. Read the file metadata using the file handler.
2. Determine the file size and MIME type.
3. Compute whether the file can be processed by the codec according to implementation constraints.
4. Suggest a recipe from the size thresholds:
   - size < 1 KB => quick
   - size < 10 KB => light
   - size < 100 KB => classic
   - otherwise => gourmet
5. Return a map containing size, MIME type, can_process, suggested recipe, or an error state with can_process=false.
Related Features:
- fileHandler
- suggestRecipe
Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData
Input:
- filePath: path of the file to inspect.
Output:
- Returns an `EMap` containing file size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe.
- On error, returns a map with `can_process=false` and error details.
Pre-condition:
- `filePath` must not be null.
- The file should exist and be readable, unless error reporting is expected.
Post-condition:
- The returned map reflects the file metadata or the failure state.
- No file content is altered.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Summary:
Restore raw bytes from a map representation of prepared binary data.
Algorithm:
1. Read the `content`, `mime_type`, and `size` entries from the map.
2. Validate that `content` is present and Base64-encoded.
3. Convert the map into a prepared-data equivalent structure if needed.
4. Base64-decode `content` and return the raw bytes.
Related Features:
- restoreBinaryData
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
- data: map containing serialized binary payload fields.
- Expected field names: `content`, `mime_type`, `size`.
Output:
- Returns the restored raw byte array.
Pre-condition:
- `data` must not be null.
- The map must contain valid binary payload fields.
Post-condition:
- The decoded bytes are equivalent to the original raw data.
- The input map is not modified.

EmojiCodec::unprocessData
Summary:
Reverse the configured compression transform on a byte array after emoji decoding.
Algorithm:
1. If compression mode is `none`, return the input bytes unchanged.
2. If compression mode is `zlib`, decompress the byte array using standard zlib-compatible decompression.
3. Return the restored byte array.
Related Features:
- compression
- compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input:
- data: processed byte array to restore.
Output:
- Returns the original uncompressed bytes.
Pre-condition:
- `data` must not be null.
- The byte array must be a valid input for the selected decompression method.
Post-condition:
- The returned bytes are suitable for text decoding or binary restoration.
- The original input is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.
```

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.

    return result;
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Perform a file-oriented encode or decode workflow and optionally write output to a path.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Inspect the requested operation (`encode` or `decode`).
   * 2. Read the input file content through the file handler.
   * 3. For encoding, convert file bytes to an emoji string; for decoding, convert emoji content back to bytes.
   * 4. If an output path is provided, write the transformed bytes to the target file, creating missing parent directories.
   * 5. Return a map containing workflow results and metadata such as byte counts and MIME type.
   * Related Features:
   * - fileHandler
   * - encodeBinary
   * - decodeBinary
   * - suggestRecipe
   * Related Classes: FileHandler, FileData, PreparedData
   * Input:
   * - inputPath: source file path.
   * - outputPath: destination file path.
   * - operation: workflow selector, typically `encode` or `decode`.
   * Output:
   * - Returns an `EMap` describing the file processing result, including relevant sizes and MIME type.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - `inputPath` must not be null.
   * - `operation` must be a supported workflow keyword.
   * - If writing output, `outputPath` must be valid or writable.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The specified file workflow is completed or an error result is returned.
   * - Output files are written only when requested and feasible.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, Object> processFile(final String inputPath, final String outputPath, final String operation)
  {
    Map<String, Object> result = new HashMap<String, Object>();
    if (inputPath == null || operation == null)
    {
      throw new NullPointerException();
    }
    FileData fileData = getFileHandler().readFile(inputPath);
    if ("encode".equalsIgnoreCase(operation))
    {
      String encoded = encodeBinary(fileData.getMimeType(), fileData.getContent());
      result.put("operation", "encode");
      result.put("encoded", encoded);
      result.put("mime_type", fileData.getMimeType());
      result.put("size", Integer.valueOf(fileData.getContent() == null ? 0 : fileData.getContent().length));
      if (outputPath != null)
      {
        getFileHandler().writeFile(outputPath, encoded.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
      }
    }
    else if ("decode".equalsIgnoreCase(operation))
    {
      EList<Object> decoded = decodeBinary(new String(fileData.getContent(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
      byte[] bytes = (byte[])decoded.get(0);
      String mimeType = (String)decoded.get(1);
      result.put("operation", "decode");
      result.put("content", bytes);
      result.put("mime_type", mimeType);
      result.put("size", decoded.get(2));
      if (outputPath != null)
      {
        getFileHandler().writeFile(outputPath, bytes);
      }
    }
    else
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unsupported operation: " + operation);
    }
    return result;
    
  }

    if (filePath == null)
    {
      throw new NullPointerException();
    }
    try
    {
      FileData fileData = getFileHandler().readFile(filePath);
      int size = fileData.getContent() == null ? 0 : fileData.getContent().length;

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Apply the configured compression transform to a byte array before emoji chunk mapping.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If compression mode is `none`, return the input bytes unchanged.
   * 2. If compression mode is `zlib`, compress the input using standard zlib-compatible compression.
   * 3. Return the processed byte array.
   * Related Features:
   * - compression
   * - compressionMethod
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: byte array to process.
   * Output:
   * - Returns compressed bytes when `zlib` is selected, otherwise the original bytes.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - `data` must not be null.
   * - The compression mode must be one of the supported methods.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The returned bytes are safe to feed into emoji chunk encoding.
   * - The original input is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public byte[] processData(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new NullPointerException("data");
    }
    if (getCompression() == null || "none".equalsIgnoreCase(getCompression()))
    {
      return data;
    }
    if ("zlib".equalsIgnoreCase(getCompression()))
    {
      Deflater deflater = new Deflater();
      deflater.setInput(data);
      deflater.finish();
      ByteArrayOutputStream out = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
      byte[] buffer = new byte[1024];
      while (!deflater.finished())
      {
        int count = deflater.deflate(buffer);
        out.write(buffer, 0, count);
      }
      deflater.end();
      return out.toByteArray();
    }
    throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported compression mode: " + getCompression());
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Reverse the configured compression transform on a byte array after emoji decoding.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If compression mode is `none`, return the input bytes unchanged.
   * 2. If compression mode is `zlib`, decompress the byte array using standard zlib-compatible decompression.
   * 3. Return the restored byte array.
   * Related Features:
   * - compression
   * - compressionMethod
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: processed byte array to restore.
   * Output:
   * - Returns the original uncompressed bytes.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - `data` must not be null.
   * - The byte array must be a valid input for the selected decompression method.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The returned bytes are suitable for text decoding or binary restoration.
   * - The original input is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public byte[] unprocessData(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new NullPointerException("data");
    }
    if (getCompression() == null || "none".equalsIgnoreCase(getCompression()))
    {
      return data;
    }
    if ("zlib".equalsIgnoreCase(getCompression()))
    {
      Inflater inflater = new Inflater();
      inflater.setInput(data);
      ByteArrayOutputStream out = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
      byte[] buffer = new byte[1024];
      try
      {
        while (!inflater.finished())
        {
          int count = inflater.inflate(buffer);
          if (count == 0 && inflater.needsInput())
          {
            break;
          }
          out.write(buffer, 0, count);
        }
      }
      catch (Exception e)
      {
        throw new RuntimeException(e);
      }
      finally
      {
        inflater.end();
      }
      return out.toByteArray();
    }
    throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported compression mode: " + getCompression());
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Calculate a SHA-256 hash digest for the given binary data and return it as a lowercase hexadecimal string.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If verification mode is `none`, return an empty string.
   * 2. Otherwise, compute SHA-256 over the input byte array.
   * 3. Convert each digest byte to a two-character lowercase hexadecimal representation with zero padding.
   * 4. Concatenate all hex pairs and return the resulting 64-character string.
   * Related Features:
   * - verification
   * - verificationMethod
   * Related Classes: VerificationMethod
   * Input:
   * - data: binary content to hash, as `EByteArray`.
   * - If data is empty, the hash is still computed over an empty byte sequence.
   * Output:
   * - Returns a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string.
   * - Returns `""` when verification is disabled (`none`).
   * Pre-condition:
   * - The input byte array must not be null.
   * - The codec must have a valid verification mode configured.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The returned string is deterministic for the same input data.
   * - No state of the codec is modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public String calculateHash(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new NullPointerException("data");
    }
    if (getVerification() == null || "none".equalsIgnoreCase(getVerification()))
    {
      return "";
    }
    if ("sha256".equalsIgnoreCase(getVerification()))
    {
      try
      {
        MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
        byte[] hash = digest.digest(data);
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (byte b : hash)
        {
          sb.append(String.format("%02x", Integer.valueOf(b & 0xFF)));
        }
        return sb.toString();
      }
      catch (Exception e)
      {
        throw new RuntimeException(e);
      }
    }
    throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported verification mode: " + getVerification());
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Suggest an emoji recipe name based on file size thresholds.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If size is less than 1 KB, return `quick`.
   * 2. Else if size is less than 10 KB, return `light`.
   * 3. Else if size is less than 100 KB, return `classic`.
   * 4. Otherwise return `gourmet`.
   * Related Features:
   * - None
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input:
   * - size: file size in bytes.
   * - Must be interpreted as a non-negative integer.
   * Output:
   * - Returns one of: `quick`, `light`, `classic`, `gourmet`.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - `size` must be greater than or equal to 0.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The suggested recipe corresponds to the configured thresholds.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public String suggestRecipe(final int size)
  {
    if (size < 1024)
    {
      return "quick";
    }
    if (size < 10240)
    {
      return "light";
    }
    if (size < 102400)
    {
      return "classic";
    }
    return "gourmet";
    
  }

```java
  public EList<Map<String, Object>> batchProcess(final String filePattern, final String outputDir, final String operation)
  {
      try {
            Path outDir = Path.of(outputDir);
            Files.createDirectories(outDir);
    
            Path patternPath = Path.of(filePattern);
            Path directory = patternPath.getParent();
    
            if (directory == null) {
                directory = Path.of(".");
            }
    
            String glob = patternPath.getFileName().toString();
    
            PathMatcher matcher = directory
                .getFileSystem()
                .getPathMatcher("glob:" + glob);
    
            BasicEList<Path> files = new BasicEList<Path>();
    
            try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream =
                    Files.newDirectoryStream(directory)) {
    
                for (Path entry : stream) {
                    if (Files.isRegularFile(entry)
                            && matcher.matches(entry.getFileName())) {
                        files.add(entry);
                    }
                }
            }
    
            BasicEList<Map<String, Object>> results =
                new BasicEList<Map<String, Object>>();
    
            for (Path inputFile : files) {
                String stem = inputFile.getFileName().toString();
                int dotIndex = stem.lastIndexOf('.');
    
                if (dotIndex > 0) {
                    stem = stem.substring(0, dotIndex);
                }
    
                Path outputPath;
    
                if ("encode".equals(operation)) {
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(stem + ".emoji");
                } else {
                    String mimeType =
                        URLConnection.guessContentTypeFromName(
                            inputFile.getFileName().toString()
                        );
    
                    String extension =
                        mimeType != null ? ".bin" : ".bin";
    
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(
                        "decoded_" + stem + extension
                    );
                }
    
                try {
                    Map<String, Object> statistics = processFile(
                        inputFile.toString(),
                        outputPath.toString(),
                        operation
                    );
    
                    statistics.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    statistics.put("success", Boolean.TRUE);
    
                    results.add(statistics);
                } catch (Exception exception) {
                    Map<String, Object> errorResult =
                        new LinkedHashMap<String, Object>();
    
                    errorResult.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    errorResult.put("success", Boolean.FALSE);
                    errorResult.put("error", exception.getMessage());
    
                    results.add(errorResult);
                }
            }
    
            return results;
        } catch (IOException exception) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Batch processing error: " + exception.getMessage(),
                exception
            );
        }
  }
```

```java
  {
      try {
            Path outDir = Path.of(outputDir);
            Files.createDirectories(outDir);
    
            Path patternPath = Path.of(filePattern);
            Path directory = patternPath.getParent();
    
            if (directory == null) {
                directory = Path.of(".");
            }
    
            String glob = patternPath.getFileName().toString();
    
            PathMatcher matcher = directory
                .getFileSystem()
                .getPathMatcher("glob:" + glob);
    
            BasicEList<Path> files = new BasicEList<Path>();
    
            try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream =
                    Files.newDirectoryStream(directory)) {
    
                for (Path entry : stream) {
                    if (Files.isRegularFile(entry)
                            && matcher.matches(entry.getFileName())) {
                        files.add(entry);
                    }
                }
            }
    
            BasicEList<Map<String, Object>> results =
                new BasicEList<Map<String, Object>>();
    
            for (Path inputFile : files) {
                String stem = inputFile.getFileName().toString();
                int dotIndex = stem.lastIndexOf('.');
    
                if (dotIndex > 0) {
                    stem = stem.substring(0, dotIndex);
                }
    
                Path outputPath;
    
                if ("encode".equals(operation)) {
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(stem + ".emoji");
                } else {
                    String mimeType =
                        URLConnection.guessContentTypeFromName(
                            inputFile.getFileName().toString()
                        );
    
                    String extension =
                        mimeType != null ? ".bin" : ".bin";
    
                    outputPath = outDir.resolve(
                        "decoded_" + stem + extension
                    );
                }
    
                try {
                    Map<String, Object> statistics = processFile(
                        inputFile.toString(),
                        outputPath.toString(),
                        operation
                    );
    
                    statistics.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    statistics.put("success", Boolean.TRUE);
    
                    results.add(statistics);
                } catch (Exception exception) {
                    Map<String, Object> errorResult =
                        new LinkedHashMap<String, Object>();
    
                    errorResult.put("file", inputFile.toString());
                    errorResult.put("success", Boolean.FALSE);
                    errorResult.put("error", exception.getMessage());
    
                    results.add(errorResult);
                }
            }
    
            return results;
        } catch (IOException exception) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Batch processing error: " + exception.getMessage(),
                exception
            );
        }
  }
```

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
